If task switching works elsewhere, focus on the affected title’s display settings, file verification and official support notes. Preserve local saves, mods and configuration files before resetting anything. A system-wide driver reinstall is disproportionate when one title has a corrupt preference or unsupported fullscreen combination.

If every fullscreen application fails in the same way, the Windows display path, driver, monitor configuration or shared overlay becomes more likely. That still does not identify a single cause. Retain the same resolution and monitor during comparisons. Benchmark applications and stress tests add load and can introduce different failure modes, so they should not replace a simple, repeatable task-switching check.

sections.heading: Create a concise support packet without exposing private data
paragraphs: For a persistent case, record the game, launcher, Windows version, graphics adapter, driver provider and version, monitor model, cable type, resolution, refresh rate, HDR state, display mode and exact Alt-Tab sequence. State whether audio continues and whether Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B restores the image. List each single change and its result rather than summarizing several actions as one fix.

Send the packet through the game, PC or graphics vendor’s official support route. Review screenshots and diagnostic files for account names, device names, serial numbers and unrelated applications before sharing. Never include credentials or authentication codes. Precise observations let support distinguish a game-specific fullscreen problem from a Windows, driver or external-display issue without forcing the user to repeat risky, undocumented changes.

sections.heading: Retest, restore and stop when hardware safety is uncertain
paragraphs: A credible improvement should survive several repetitions and an ordinary restart. Confirm the final resolution, refresh rate, display mode, HDR state, driver version and connected screens. Restore every experimental change that did not contribute. Leaving HDR, monitor routing and per-game graphics preferences altered without a record may hide the original symptom while creating color, performance or power problems later.

Stop testing if a cable or port becomes hot, the display repeatedly loses power, Windows reports a hardware error, or unrelated applications also fail after a clean restart. Power down equipment according to its manual and contact the manufacturer. Do not continue reconnecting damaged hardware or attempt firmware changes based only on a black screen after Alt-Tab. Safety and preserved evidence matter more than completing every checklist item.

items.title: PC Game Controller Not Detected in Windows: A Safe Troubleshooting Checklist
items.dek: A reversible, evidence-first path for USB and Bluetooth controllers that disappear, connect incorrectly or work in Windows but not inside one game.
items.author: Eli Morgan
items.imageAlt: Original editorial illustration of a PC game controller passing through USB, Bluetooth and Windows device checks
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific editorial artwork generated in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original deterministic artwork with no third-party logos or game assets
body: When a game controller is not detected, begin by deciding where detection stops: physical connection, Windows, the launcher or one game. Test a known data cable, direct USB port and the Windows controller panel before changing drivers. For Bluetooth, confirm charge, range and pairing, then remove and add the device only if the existing entry will not connect.

A lit controller is not proof that data is flowing, and a controller visible in Windows is not proof that one game has selected it. This guide keeps those layers separate, uses reversible tests and protects game saves and profiles. Change one variable, repeat the same test and record the result.

The steps rely on current Microsoft support guidance for Bluetooth, USB and Device Manager. Hardware-maker and game-specific instructions remain authoritative. Stop if a battery is swollen, a connector overheats or a cable is damaged.
takeaways: Use a known data cable and a direct USB port before changing drivers.
Separate USB, Bluetooth, Windows and game-specific tests.
Record Device Manager errors before uninstalling one targeted device.
Back up profiles and settings before resets; never delete save folders for an input issue.
Cross-test one controller and one known-good system before concluding hardware has failed.

sections.heading: Start with a symptom you can reproduce
paragraphs: Write down whether the controller is absent everywhere, visible in Windows but ignored by one game, detected only by cable, or disconnected after sleep. Test one known game and the Windows controller panel without changing drivers first. A precise symptom prevents random fixes from creating several new variables.

Note the controller model, connection type, Windows version, game launcher and the last time it worked. If the failure began after an update, dock change or new USB device, record that fact without assuming causation. The goal is a baseline that can be retested after each reversible step.

sections.heading: Check power, cable and the physical port
paragraphs: Charge the controller or install known-good batteries. For a wired test, use a data-capable cable; some USB cables deliver power but do not carry data. Connect directly to the computer rather than through a hub, monitor or dock. Microsoft’s USB guidance recommends checking the connection and trying an appropriate port.

Inspect the connector for looseness or damage without forcing it. Try one other port, then return to the original configuration if there is no change. Do not buy accessories until a simple direct connection has been tested. A controller lighting up proves power, not successful data communication.

sections.heading: Separate USB from Bluetooth diagnosis
paragraphs: A controller that works by cable but not wirelessly has already passed several hardware and game checks. Focus on Bluetooth pairing, range, interference and the computer’s radio. Conversely, a Bluetooth connection does not prove the USB cable carries data. Treat the two paths as separate tests.

Microsoft advises turning Bluetooth off and on, confirming the device is charged and in range, and checking interference from nearby USB 3.0 equipment. Perform those steps in a controlled order. Keep the wired path available so you can distinguish a wireless problem from a game-specific input problem.

sections.heading: Remove and pair again only after preserving the baseline
paragraphs: If the controller appears in the Bluetooth list but will not connect, Microsoft recommends removing the device and adding it again. Before doing so, photograph the current device name and status. Remove only the intended controller; do not clear every paired device as a first response.

Put the controller into its documented pairing mode and keep it close to the computer. Wait for Windows to finish adding it before launching a game. If several devices share similar names, turn off the others temporarily. Repeated pairing attempts without removing a stale entry can make the result harder to interpret.

sections.heading: Use Device Manager as evidence, not as a deletion tool
paragraphs: Open Device Manager and inspect Human Interface Devices, Bluetooth and sound or game-controller categories. A warning icon or error code provides a more specific route than guessing. Microsoft documents Device Manager codes and advises following the resolution associated with the code.

Do not uninstall multiple USB controllers, chipset devices or Bluetooth adapters at once. If a single controller entry clearly shows an error, record its properties before changing it. Scan for hardware changes after a targeted action. A missing entry points toward connection or enumeration; a healthy entry shifts attention to game configuration.

sections.heading: Update through Windows and the hardware maker
paragraphs: Install pending Windows updates and use the controller manufacturer’s official application or support page for firmware. Avoid third-party driver bundles. Generic controllers may use drivers already included with Windows, while branded devices may require a supported accessory app for firmware and profiles.

Create a restore point when appropriate and change one layer at a time. Reboot after a driver or firmware change if the official instructions require it. Then repeat the same baseline test. An update that installs successfully is not proof of repair until Windows and the game recognise the controller consistently.

sections.heading: Test Windows input before blaming the game
paragraphs: Open the Windows game-controller test panel or the supported accessory application and confirm that buttons and axes respond. If Windows receives input correctly, the cable, radio and basic driver path are probably functioning. Continue with launcher, game and input-mode checks instead of reinstalling the entire device stack.

If Windows lists the controller but no inputs respond, test without remapping software and disconnect duplicate controllers. Record whether the problem affects every control or only one axis. Hardware calibration, profile corruption and physical wear are different faults, so a detailed input test prevents an incorrect software conclusion.

sections.heading: Eliminate duplicate and virtual controllers
paragraphs: Flight sticks, wheels, phones, remote-play tools and virtual gamepads can change the order in which a game assigns controllers. Disconnect nonessential input devices, close remapping tools and restart the game. Do not uninstall specialised software permanently until a conflict is actually demonstrated.

If the controller begins working, reconnect devices one by one to identify the conflict. Some games select the first enumerated device and offer no obvious prompt. Preserve profiles before resetting tools such as remappers. The safe objective is to identify one interfering layer, not to erase every configuration.

sections.heading: Check the game’s input mode and launcher layer
paragraphs: Some games support only specific APIs or switch between keyboard, Xbox-style and PlayStation-style prompts. Inspect the game’s official controller-support page and in-game settings. A controller can function in Windows while the title expects a different mode or has controller input disabled.

Launch the game from its normal client and test with overlays or input-translation features unchanged first. Then toggle one relevant feature, such as a supported launcher input layer, and retest. Avoid enabling several compatibility modes simultaneously because duplicate translation can produce double input or no input.

sections.heading: Verify files only when the problem is game-specific
paragraphs: If the controller works in Windows and other games but fails in one title, use that launcher’s official file-verification function. This can replace damaged game files without deleting saves, although local modifications may be affected. Back up configuration files before resetting them.

Do not verify every installed game or reinstall a large title as the first step. Compare the affected game’s input configuration with a working title. Check official patch notes and known issues. A game-specific regression requires evidence from that title’s support channel, not a generic controller replacement.

sections.heading: Inspect per-game configuration without deleting saves
paragraphs: Locate the game’s settings file only through official documentation or a reliable support article. Copy it before renaming or resetting it. Never delete the entire save directory to fix an input setting. Cloud synchronization can propagate an unwanted deletion to another computer.

After a clean configuration test, restore custom settings gradually. If the controller works only with a fresh profile, compare input bindings and device identifiers. Keep the backup until progress and preferences are confirmed. Input troubleshooting should not put saved games at risk.

sections.heading: Consider USB power management after simpler checks
paragraphs: Windows may power down some USB devices to conserve energy. If the controller disappears after sleep or during long idle periods, review power management for the relevant hub or adapter using official guidance. Record the original setting so it can be restored.

Do not disable power saving across every USB device without evidence. Test the exact scenario that caused disconnection, including sleep and wake. A controller that fails immediately at boot is unlikely to be explained solely by idle power management. Match the intervention to the observed timing.

sections.heading: Know when the evidence points to hardware
paragraphs: Test the controller on another supported computer or console and test a known-good controller on the original PC. This cross-test separates controller hardware, cable, port and computer configuration. Use supported devices and avoid interpreting one incompatible platform as a failure.

If the same controller fails across supported systems with multiple known-good cables, contact the manufacturer with the recorded symptoms and serial details. Stop using a swollen battery, damaged cable or overheating device. Software troubleshooting should not continue when there is a physical safety concern.

sections.heading: Finish with a stable retest and a short record
paragraphs: Reboot once, connect the controller using the chosen method, open the Windows input test and play the same game section used at the start. Confirm reconnection after sleep if that was part of the problem. A repair is credible only when the symptom no longer reproduces.

Write down the successful step, driver or firmware version and any setting changed. Remove temporary tools and reconnect other devices gradually. If the problem returns, the record avoids repeating risky actions and gives support staff a clear sequence rather than a vague description.

sections.heading: Build a clean support packet before escalating
paragraphs: If the controller still fails, prepare a compact support packet rather than repeating resets. Include the controller model, connection method, Windows edition and build, firmware version, Device Manager status, the games tested and the exact point where detection stops. Add the results of the cross-test with another cable, port or supported system. Redact account names, serial numbers and personal paths from screenshots before posting them publicly.

Contact the controller maker when the device fails across supported systems, the computer maker when several known-good USB devices fail on the same ports, or the game publisher when Windows input works but one title alone ignores it. Use official support channels and keep case numbers. A structured report shortens diagnosis and prevents an input fault from turning into unnecessary driver removal, game deletion or hardware purchases.

items.title: PC Game Crash Evidence: Logs, Dumps and a Privacy-Safe Support Report
items.dek: A controlled checklist for preserving the right Windows, launcher and reproduction evidence after a PC game crash without posting private data or changing the system before the failure is documented.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original editorial diagram showing a PC game crash timeline, Windows event record, launcher log and privacy review before a support report is sent
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original editorial artwork with no third-party logos, screenshots or game assets
body: After a PC game crashes, preserve the exact time, error message and repeatable action before reinstalling anything. Reproduce the failure once only if it is safe, then collect the game or launcher log requested by official support, note the Windows build and relevant hardware, and review every attachment for usernames, file paths, account identifiers, chat text or memory contents. Send the smallest evidence set that answers the support request through the vendor’s official private channel; never post a full dump or unreviewed system report publicly.

A useful crash report is not the largest archive a player can produce. It is a short, ordered packet that connects a specific game version and action to a specific time, symptom and diagnostic record. Windows Error Reporting can create reports for crashes and hangs, launchers can maintain their own logs, and a game may write a separate crash folder. These sources answer different questions. Mixing days of unrelated logs into one upload can hide the relevant event and expose more information than support needs.

This guide explains evidence collection, not dump analysis or registry modification. Full memory dumps and advanced debugging can be appropriate when a qualified support engineer asks for them, but they may contain private material and require careful handling. Start with visible facts and ordinary vendor-supported logs. Preserve original files, work from copies, and stop if reproducing the failure risks a save, an online penalty, hardware instability or repeated data loss.
takeaways: Write down the exact crash time and reproduction steps before changing the installation.
Collect only the official game, launcher or Windows record relevant to that time.
Treat dumps and system reports as potentially sensitive until reviewed.
Send evidence privately through the correct official support channel.
Keep an untouched local copy and a simple manifest of every attachment.

sections.heading: Freeze the timeline before troubleshooting changes the evidence
paragraphs: Record the local date and time as soon as the game closes, freezes or returns to the desktop. Copy the error text exactly instead of paraphrasing it, and note whether the process vanished, remained in Task Manager or required a forced close. Write the last action that occurred in the game, the current game and launcher versions, and whether an update had just completed. If a screenshot is safe, capture the message without including private notifications, friend lists, account names or unrelated windows. This timestamp is the key used to match a visible failure with the correct log entry.

Do not immediately verify files, reinstall the launcher, clear caches or run a registry cleaner. Those actions can rotate logs, replace binaries and erase the state that support needs to examine. Save cloud synchronization does not preserve diagnostic files. If the game can be closed normally, let the launcher finish any synchronization, then stop. When the crash follows a consistent harmless action, one controlled reproduction can confirm the time and steps. Avoid repeated reproductions when the failure corrupts saves, triggers anti-cheat warnings, overheats the machine or causes a full system restart.

sections.heading: Describe the symptom precisely before choosing a log
paragraphs: A crash to desktop, a frozen window, a launcher error, a blue screen and a spontaneous reboot are not the same event. A game that closes while Windows continues running usually calls for application-level evidence. A launcher that fails before the game starts points first to launcher records. A whole-system stop or reboot requires a different support route and may involve Windows or hardware evidence. State what remained responsive, whether audio continued, whether an error dialog appeared and how long the failure took. This description prevents a support agent from requesting a large diagnostic bundle that cannot answer the real question.

Separate performance symptoms from termination. Low frame rate, a periodic hitch and delayed input can be measured without a crash record. If the process does not exit, say that it hangs rather than crashes. Windows Error Reporting distinguishes crashes and non-response conditions, and individual games may use their own reporter. Do not rename a file to make it look like a dump or assume the newest file anywhere on the drive belongs to the incident. The evidence should share the recorded timestamp and correspond to the process that actually failed.

sections.heading: Start with the game’s own crash folder and official support instructions
paragraphs: Open the publisher’s current support article for the affected title and follow its documented location or in-game reporting tool. Some games create a text log, a small dump, configuration details and a crash identifier together; others upload a report and display only a reference code. Preserve that reference code and copy the generated folder before launching the game again. Do not collect similarly named folders from mod tools or old installations unless support specifically requests them. A title-specific reporter normally provides more relevant context than a broad system inventory.

Check the modification times inside the copied folder. The primary file should align with the crash time, while older sessions can be left out of the initial submission. Keep the original extension and filename because support automation may rely on them. Do not open binary dump files in random online viewers or upload them to public file-sharing services. If the game offers a consent screen describing what will be transmitted, read it and use the least expansive option that still meets the support request. Note in your manifest whether the report was uploaded automatically or remains only on the device.

sections.heading: Collect launcher logs only when the launcher is part of the failure
paragraphs: Epic’s official instructions tell users to enable Debug Logging, reproduce the launcher issue, use Show Logs and attach the most recent EpicGamesLauncher log to the support ticket. That procedure is designed for launcher behavior; it does not automatically prove why a separate game executable crashed after launch. Enable extra logging only for the shortest reproduction needed, then turn it off. Copy the relevant file, record its time range and keep the original locally. If the failure occurs entirely inside one game, prefer that game’s support instructions before collecting a verbose launcher history.

Steam’s official System Reports documentation explains that a report describes the machine’s hardware and software configuration for support review. A system report is supporting context, not a replacement for the crash time, error and game-specific log. Generate it only when Steam Support or the publisher requests that level of configuration detail. Before attaching it, read the visible text for account identifiers, device names, storage paths or unrelated software you do not need to disclose. Never paste a complete system report into a public forum merely because it is text rather than a dump.

sections.heading: Use Windows application events as a timestamped clue, not a verdict
paragraphs: When a game closes unexpectedly on Windows, an Application log entry near the recorded time can identify the failing executable, event type or faulting module. Open Event Viewer through Windows search, inspect Windows Logs and Application, and match the entry by time and process name. Save or copy only the relevant event details requested by support. An event naming a module is evidence that the fault surfaced there; it is not automatic proof that the module caused the original problem. Drivers, overlays, corrupted data and the game itself can all influence where a failure becomes visible.

Avoid clearing any log before the case is resolved. Do not export the entire Security log or days of system events for a game ticket. If Event Viewer contains no matching application event, say so instead of selecting a nearby warning from an unrelated service. A clean timeline is more valuable than a dramatic error with the wrong timestamp. Record the event source, ID, faulting application and faulting module exactly when present, but leave interpretation to the game publisher or qualified support team unless an official knowledge-base article maps that exact event to a confirmed cause.

sections.heading: Understand what Windows Error Reporting can and cannot show
paragraphs: Microsoft documents Windows Error Reporting as the Windows infrastructure for reporting crashes, non-response conditions and kernel faults. A report can contain information needed to classify the failure, and applications may also implement their own reporting. The existence of a WER record confirms that Windows detected an event; it does not guarantee that a usable local dump was produced or that every game routes failures through WER. Search by the recorded time and application name, and follow official support instructions for any report identifier or file that should be supplied.

Microsoft also documents LocalDumps configuration for collecting user-mode dumps after an application crash, while noting exceptions for applications with custom crash reporting. That is an advanced diagnostic configuration, not a universal first step. Do not add registry settings from an anonymous guide simply to make a larger file. If official support requests a local dump, ask which executable, dump type and retention period they require, document the change and remove temporary collection settings after the requested reproduction. Keep sufficient free storage and never assume that a missing dump means no crash occurred.

sections.heading: Treat crash dumps and diagnostic archives as sensitive files
paragraphs: A dump can include process memory, paths, loaded modules and fragments of data that were in use when the application failed. Microsoft’s Windows privacy guidance distinguishes basic crash information from the crash-dump content itself and notes that sending dump content involves additional permission in Windows diagnostic settings. An archive can also contain the Windows username, device name, account identifiers, command lines or text from overlays and chat tools. File size does not measure privacy risk: a small minidump can still reveal more context than a normal screenshot.

Review text logs with a plain local editor and search for your email address, real name, Windows account folder, IP address, session tokens, license keys and chat content. Do not edit the only original; make a redacted copy and list every redaction so support understands the change. Do not attempt to sanitize a binary dump with a text editor because that can corrupt it without reliably removing private material. If a dump is required, send it only through the vendor’s authenticated private ticket or approved secure upload and ask about retention when the case involves especially sensitive data.

sections.heading: Build a minimal manifest that makes every attachment useful
paragraphs: Create a short text file with the ticket subject, crash time and time zone, game version, launcher version, Windows build, GPU model and driver version, exact reproduction steps, expected result and actual result. List each attachment with its filename, source and matching time. Mark whether the file is original, copied or redacted. Include the crash reporter reference code when one exists. This manifest lets support verify that a launcher log, application event and game crash folder all describe the same incident rather than three unrelated sessions.

Keep the hardware list relevant. A controller model matters for an input crash; a complete inventory of printers and unrelated storage devices usually does not. State recent changes factually: game update, driver update, mod removal or overlay setting change. Do not claim causation merely because two events occurred on the same day. If mods are installed, say so and record the tested state; do not hide them from support or upload third-party mod files. For online games, mention whether the failure occurred before authentication, in a menu or during a specific match type without exposing another player’s personal information.

sections.heading: Send the report through the correct official channel
paragraphs: Use the affected game publisher’s authenticated support portal when the failure is limited to one title. Use launcher support when the launcher cannot download, update or start the game, and use the relevant hardware or Windows support route when the whole system fails. Confirm the destination domain before uploading. A social-media reply, public community post or unsolicited direct message is not an appropriate place for dumps, logs or system reports. If support provides a case-specific upload link, verify that it belongs to the official vendor and that the case number matches.

Begin with the manifest, visible error and smallest relevant logs. Offer the dump rather than attaching it automatically when its size or sensitivity is high. If the portal rejects the archive, do not split it across random public hosts. Ask support for the approved transfer method and retention limits. Preserve the ticket confirmation and the exact files sent. Support may request a second controlled reproduction with added logging; treat that as a new evidence set with a new timestamp instead of overwriting the first one.

sections.heading: Preserve a clean archive and stop collecting when the case is reproducible
paragraphs: Store the evidence in a dated folder outside the game installation: manifest, screenshots, relevant text logs, exported application event and any vendor-generated crash package. Keep original files read-only when practical and make working copies for redaction. A simple checksum can confirm that a large dump was not changed during transfer, but it does not prove that the contents are safe to share. Back up irreplaceable saves separately; diagnostic evidence and save protection are different tasks. Delete temporary public links immediately if one was created contrary to the preferred private workflow.

Once the report demonstrates a stable reproduction and support has acknowledged the files, stop gathering broad telemetry. More logging can consume storage, expose unrelated activity and make the next incident harder to isolate. Disable temporary debug logging and any support-requested dump collection according to the vendor’s instructions, while preserving the submitted packet until the ticket closes. Record the final workaround or fix and its version. If the crash returns after a later update, create a new timestamped packet instead of presenting an old log as evidence of the new failure.

items.title: PC Game Crashes After a Graphics Driver Update: A Safe Recovery Guide
items.dek: A controlled way to separate a bad driver install from a game update, unstable overclock, damaged cache or hardware fault—and roll back without making the diagnosis worse.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original editorial image of a gaming PC, frozen game screen and graphics-driver rollback timeline
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original editorial artwork with no third-party logos or game assets
body: If a PC game starts crashing immediately after a graphics-driver update, first record the old and new driver versions, restart Windows once, and reproduce the failure with the same game settings. Disable only optional overlays and any GPU overclock for the test. If the timing strongly implicates the update, use Windows Device Manager's Roll Back Driver option when available, or reinstall a known-good package downloaded from the GPU manufacturer's official site. Do not download drivers from third-party aggregators.

The phrase “the new driver broke my game” may be correct, but timing alone is not proof. A game patch, Windows update, anti-cheat change, shader-cache rebuild, unstable memory profile or failing power connection can appear in the same session. Changing several things at once destroys the comparison that would identify the cause. The safest recovery is therefore a short evidence-led sequence: preserve the error, establish a baseline, remove optional variables, then roll back or reinstall through documented channels.

This guide applies to ordinary Windows gaming PCs using supported NVIDIA or AMD graphics hardware. It does not recommend modified packages, registry cleaners, firmware flashing or tools from unknown publishers. Manufacturer utilities and Windows recovery features can change over time, so the linked Microsoft, NVIDIA and AMD pages remain the primary references. If the computer shows artifacts before Windows loads, shuts off under load, smells hot, or has a damaged power connector, stop software troubleshooting and inspect the hardware safely.
takeaways: Confirm the regression with the same game, save, settings and workload before changing more software.
Record driver and game versions, the exact crash message and whether other 3D applications fail.
Use Windows rollback or an official vendor installer; avoid third-party driver sites and blanket registry fixes.
Treat artifacts, power loss and failures outside games as possible hardware problems rather than forcing repeated installs.

sections.heading: Before rollback: prove what actually changed
paragraphs: Write down the installed graphics-driver version, its installation date, the game build, Windows build and the last known combination that worked. In Windows, the Display adapters entry in Device Manager exposes the Driver tab and version details. The game launcher or main menu normally shows the game build. Save the exact crash code, a screenshot and the time of the event. These facts turn “it crashes now” into a version pair that a developer or GPU vendor can reproduce.

Check the timeline for other changes. Did the game patch on the same day? Did Windows restart to finish an update? Was a new overlay, capture tool, anti-cheat component or hardware-monitoring utility installed? A coincident change does not clear the graphics driver, but it prevents premature certainty. Do not clear Windows logs, wipe caches or reinstall the game before collecting the first clean reproduction. Those actions can remove evidence and add new variables.

sections.heading: Create one repeatable crash test
paragraphs: Choose the smallest sequence that reliably triggers the problem: load one save, enter one area, start one benchmark or wait at one menu. Keep resolution, graphics preset, API selection and frame cap unchanged. Restart Windows, stop downloads, then run that sequence once. Note whether the crash happens before the game renders, during shader preparation, at the same scene, or only after the GPU has been under load for several minutes.

Test one other trusted 3D application or game, preferably one that worked before the update. If only a single title fails, a game-specific regression, damaged game file or API interaction is more plausible. If several unrelated 3D applications fail in the same way, the driver installation, system stability or hardware moves higher on the list. Do not use an hour-long stress test when a two-minute game sequence already reproduces the fault; repeated hard crashes can corrupt open files.

sections.heading: Return clocks and overlays to a neutral baseline
paragraphs: A driver can change boost behavior, shader compilation or memory use enough to expose an overclock that appeared stable before. Restore the GPU and video memory to their manufacturer defaults. If a CPU or memory overclock is easy to disable through a documented profile, record the existing configuration before testing the default. Do not change voltages or update firmware as a first response. The objective is to test a supported baseline, not to tune around an unknown fault.

Temporarily disable optional overlays one at a time: recording, performance monitoring, chat overlays and frame injectors can hook into the graphics path. Keep security software and anti-cheat enabled unless the relevant publisher explicitly instructs otherwise. If removing a specific overlay stops the crash on the same driver and route, re-enable it once to confirm the relationship, then update or report that component. A mass “clean boot” may hide the cause without identifying it.

sections.heading: Check temperature, power and visible artifacts
paragraphs: Driver timing can reveal a marginal power or thermal problem, but software cannot repair a loose cable or overheating card. Watch for colored blocks, sparkling pixels, corrupted geometry, black screens outside the game, sudden restarts or a complete power loss. A normal application crash that returns to the desktop is different from a machine that shuts down. Log temperatures and clocks with one reputable tool, and compare them with the hardware maker's published guidance rather than a random universal limit.

Power down and disconnect the computer before touching internal hardware. If you are qualified to inspect it, check that the card is seated and that power connectors are fully engaged without visible heat damage. Do not repeatedly boot a system with a scorched connector or burning smell. Laptops and warranty-covered desktops should generally be handled through the manufacturer. If artifacts are visible in firmware screens or before the graphics driver loads, a Windows rollback is unlikely to be the complete solution.

sections.heading: Use Windows Roll Back Driver when it is available
paragraphs: Microsoft documents rollback through Device Manager: expand Display adapters, open the GPU's Properties, choose the Driver tab, select Roll Back Driver, give the requested reason and restart. Administrator permission is required. The button can be unavailable when Windows no longer retains the previous package, when the driver was replaced through another installation method, or when storage cleanup removed rollback files. Its absence is not proof that no earlier driver exists.

After the restart, confirm the actual version rather than assuming the rollback succeeded. Repeat the same short game route with the same settings. If the crash disappears, preserve the working configuration and report the version pair to the game or GPU vendor. Do not immediately reinstall the failing version just to make the system current. First check its release notes, known issues and whether a newer hotfix or game patch addresses the regression.

sections.heading: If rollback is unavailable, reinstall an official known-good package
paragraphs: Download the intended driver directly from the official NVIDIA driver page or AMD support page. Match the operating system, GPU family and architecture. Laptop owners should also check the computer manufacturer's support page because some models use customized power, display-switching or thermal components. Verify that the file publisher is the expected vendor before running it. Avoid mirror sites, “driver updater” subscriptions and repackaged installers.

Close games and creative applications, preserve open work, and use the vendor installer's documented options. A normal reinstall is often enough; “clean install” is not inherently safer and resets profiles that may be useful evidence. Restart when requested, confirm the version, then repeat the same reproduction route. Do not install several historical packages in succession. One controlled known-good comparison is more informative than cycling through a stack of versions.

sections.heading: Reserve cleanup utilities for a failed or corrupted install
paragraphs: A cleanup tool is justified when the official installer fails, Device Manager shows an error, driver components are visibly mixed, or a normal reinstall cannot complete. AMD's official Cleanup Utility is designed to remove previously installed AMD graphics and audio driver software while leaving AMD chipset software in place. Follow the vendor's instructions, including its Safe Mode recommendation where applicable, and create a restore point or backup first.

Do not treat any third-party removal utility as a mandatory gaming ritual. Deep removal changes more state, can erase profiles and complicates support if the original failure was game-specific. For NVIDIA hardware, use NVIDIA's official installation guidance and support channels rather than assuming an AMD procedure applies. Disconnecting the internet to prevent Windows Update interference may be recommended in a particular official workflow, but should not become a permanent configuration. Reconnect and restore normal updates after the controlled install.

sections.heading: Understand shader caches after a driver change
paragraphs: A new graphics driver can invalidate or rebuild cached shader and pipeline data. The first launch may therefore stutter, spend longer on a preparation screen, or compile work again. That behavior is not the same as a repeatable crash, but interrupting preparation or repeatedly deleting caches can make the first-run cost recur. Let explicit shader compilation finish, then compare the first and second run before deciding that the cache is damaged.

Delete a cache only when the game or vendor documents that step for corruption, and remove the narrowest relevant cache. Record what you deleted so the result can be interpreted. Never download another person's cache for a different GPU, driver or game build. For a deeper method, GAMIC News' shader-compilation guide explains how to compare first-use hitches with storage, CPU and frame-pacing problems without turning cache deletion into an automatic remedy.

sections.heading: Repair game files only after the driver comparison
paragraphs: If rollback does not change the result and only one game fails, use the storefront's verify or repair function before reinstalling the entire title. Verification can restore damaged executable or data files while preserving most of the installation. Back up local saves and custom files using the game's supported method. Mods, ReShade-style injectors and altered DLL files should be documented and removed through their own supported uninstall process for a clean test.

Check the game's official known-issues page, patch notes and support forum for the exact driver version and error signature. Be cautious with community fixes that replace system DLLs, disable certificate checks or ask users to turn off security protections. A launch option supplied by the developer to switch between DirectX versions can be a useful diagnostic, but changing the graphics API also changes cache and feature behavior, so record the result instead of presenting it as a universal fix.

sections.heading: Use System Restore only for a broader system regression
paragraphs: Microsoft System Restore can return system files, registry settings and installed programs to a selected restore point without targeting personal files. It is broader than a driver rollback and may undo unrelated application changes, so review the affected programs before proceeding. Use it when the failure extends beyond the graphics package or when a documented restore point cleanly predates a cluster of system changes. Back up important work first even though personal files are not the intended target.

A restore point is not a substitute for identifying a failing component. After recovery, confirm the graphics version and repeat the same test before allowing multiple pending updates to install. If the game works, reintroduce changes in a controlled order. If the machine still crashes across applications, stop repeating restore operations and investigate memory, storage, power and GPU health with the hardware vendor or a qualified technician.

sections.heading: Build a useful crash report for the vendor
paragraphs: A concise report should include GPU model, desktop or laptop model, Windows build, old and new driver versions, game build, storefront, graphics API, exact settings, crash message and a short reproduction route. State whether the problem affects other 3D applications, whether default clocks change the result, and whether rollback restores stability. Attach a small relevant log or dump only when the support instructions request it, and remove account names or personal paths where practical.

Report the regression to the party best placed to act. A failure confined to one game belongs with the developer as well as the GPU vendor; failures across several applications belong primarily with the driver vendor or system maker. Do not label a correlation as proven if the comparison is incomplete. “Driver 600.00 crashes build X at step Y; driver 599.50 does not on the same settings” is actionable. “Latest drivers are broken” is not.

sections.heading: A safe decision tree
paragraphs: If the crash began after an update, first reproduce it and record versions. If optional overlays or an overclock are involved, test the supported baseline. If several games fail and rollback is available, roll back through Device Manager and repeat the route. If rollback is unavailable, install one known-good package from the official source. If the installer is corrupted or incomplete, use the vendor's documented cleanup path. If only one game still fails, verify its files and consult its known issues.

Stop software experimentation when the evidence points to hardware: artifacts outside the game, power loss, thermal shutdown, damaged connectors or errors that persist across clean supported driver versions. Also stop when a stable known-good driver restores the machine; there is no prize for forcing a problematic release back onto it. Keep automatic updates under normal supported control, watch for a corrected release, and retain the clear versioned report that made the recovery trustworthy.

items.title: PC Game Lag Checklist: Ping, Packet Loss, Wi-Fi and Server Evidence
items.dek: A controlled way to separate local Wi-Fi trouble, congestion, route instability and game-server problems before changing drivers, ports or router settings.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original editorial network diagram comparing a gaming PC, Wi-Fi router, internet route and game server with latency, jitter and packet-loss evidence
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original editorial artwork with no third-party logos, screenshots or game assets
body: When an online PC game feels delayed, first record the exact time, region, match mode and visible symptom. Test one ordinary match without downloads or streams, compare Ethernet with the same Wi-Fi connection if practical, and use the game’s own network display when available. Measure several minutes rather than trusting one speed-test number. Keep ping, jitter or frame-time spikes and packet-loss evidence separate, because a low average ping can still hide instability. Do not open ports, disable security software or reset the router until the evidence identifies a local configuration problem.

“Lag” can describe several different failures: network delay, packet loss, jitter, frame-rate drops, shader stutter, controller delay or a struggling server. Each has a different signature. If animation freezes while the network indicator remains stable, the cause may be rendering rather than the connection. If other players teleport, inputs arrive late or voice audio breaks while frame rate stays steady, network evidence becomes more relevant. A useful diagnosis changes one variable at a time and preserves the result.

This guide stays at the safe evidence-collection layer. It does not recommend bypassing a firewall, exposing a PC directly to the internet, changing DNS as a universal cure or forwarding undocumented ports. Official Microsoft, Xbox and Steam guidance shows that latency, loss and route evidence must be interpreted in context. The objective is a short comparison that tells the player, household, internet provider or game publisher where the fault most likely begins—and where the evidence is still inconclusive.
takeaways: Describe the symptom before measuring the connection.
Compare idle and busy conditions on the same device and server region.
Use Ethernet as a controlled comparison, not as proof that every Wi-Fi network is defective.
Treat one silent traceroute hop as inconclusive when later hops still answer.
Send a timestamped, privacy-reviewed evidence packet through official support.

sections.heading: Name the failure before blaming the internet connection
paragraphs: Write down what the player actually sees. Rubber-banding means the character appears to move and then snaps back. Delayed hit registration means an action is acknowledged later than expected. A disconnect is a session failure rather than merely slow response. Choppy animation can be a rendering problem even when it occurs during multiplayer play. Note whether voice chat breaks at the same moment, whether every player is affected, and whether the frame-rate counter changes. This first description determines which measurements are relevant and prevents a graphics problem from being misreported as packet loss.

Record the game build, platform launcher, selected server region, match type and local time with time zone. If the game exposes a network graph, capture it without player names, chat or account identifiers. Note whether the symptom begins at match start, appears only in crowded scenes or follows a household upload. Do not repeatedly provoke a disconnect in ranked play or any mode with penalties. One controlled observation in a safe environment is usually enough to establish a timestamp for later comparison.

sections.heading: Build a baseline while the connection is idle
paragraphs: Before changing anything, close only voluntary high-bandwidth activity such as large downloads, cloud backup jobs and video uploads, while leaving the normal router and security configuration intact. Run the game in its usual server region and observe several minutes. Record the median or ordinary latency range, the highest spikes, visible packet loss and the exact time. A single ping result is a snapshot, not a baseline. Real-time games exchange traffic continuously, so intermittent queues or radio interference can be missed by a quick general speed test.

Repeat the observation at a different time only when the symptom is intermittent. A result that worsens every evening but remains stable earlier may point toward congestion, yet it does not by itself identify whether the bottleneck is inside the home, at the access network or farther along the route. The FCC’s broadband measurements note that congestion can raise both latency and packet loss. Preserve the time series rather than presenting one best result and one worst result without context.

sections.heading: Compare Ethernet and Wi-Fi without changing five variables
paragraphs: If the PC and router make it practical, connect the same computer to the same router by Ethernet and repeat the same game region and test window. Do not simultaneously update drivers, reboot every device, change DNS and move the router; that would make the comparison impossible to interpret. A stable wired result alongside unstable Wi-Fi is evidence that the local radio path deserves attention. It is not proof that the internet provider or game server is perfect, because the wired test may use a different time or route.

For the Wi-Fi retest, record the band, distance, walls and whether the signal changes when the device moves. Xbox network guidance lists inadequate signal strength and wireless interference among possible contributors to packet loss and delay. Prefer a clear comparison over a promise that a particular frequency band will always be better. Nearby networks, Bluetooth devices, repeaters, mesh backhaul and household layout can change the result. Keep the access point’s existing security enabled throughout the test.

sections.heading: Separate latency, jitter, loss and bandwidth
paragraphs: Latency is the travel delay for a packet or round trip. Jitter is the variation between successive delays. Packet loss means some packets do not arrive. Bandwidth describes how much data can be transferred, not how consistently a small real-time flow is delivered. A connection can download quickly yet feel poor in a game because its delay jumps under load. It can also show a respectable average ping while short loss bursts disrupt movement or voice. Report each metric separately whenever the game or official diagnostic tool exposes it.

Avoid importing fixed thresholds from an unrelated service as universal gaming rules. A turn-based title, competitive shooter, cloud-streamed game and remote-play session do not have identical requirements. Xbox publishes targets for particular console and remote-play contexts, but those numbers are context-specific rather than guarantees for every PC title. The best baseline is the same game, region and device during a known-good session compared with the failing session.

sections.heading: Use PathPing as evidence, not an automatic blame tool
paragraphs: Microsoft documents PathPing as a Windows command that combines route discovery with repeated probes and calculates latency and loss statistics for intermediate hops. Run it only against an appropriate destination supplied by the game publisher or support team. A public website address may terminate at a content network unrelated to the actual match server, so a clean result there does not clear the game path. Save the command, start time and complete output as text after reviewing local device names or addresses.

Interpret intermediate loss carefully. Some routers de-prioritize or do not answer diagnostic probes while continuing to forward later traffic normally. Steam’s official network-reporting guidance warns that a hop showing apparent total loss is not necessarily the fault when subsequent hops continue responding. Consistent loss that begins at one point and remains present through the destination is more meaningful, but even that pattern should be correlated with the game timestamp and repeated before assigning responsibility.

sections.heading: Read Tracert asterisks without inventing a broken hop
paragraphs: Microsoft’s Tracert documentation explains that some routers do not return the expected time-exceeded messages and therefore appear as asterisks. That absence is not automatically packet loss affecting the game. Look at whether later hops answer and whether the destination is reachable. A route can also change between tests because providers balance traffic. Keep one or two timestamped traces rather than running dozens and selecting the most dramatic path.

Traceroute data can reveal public IP addresses and network geography. Review output before posting it publicly, and prefer a private official ticket when the publisher asks for route evidence. Do not run aggressive third-party scanners or probe arbitrary game infrastructure. Standard operating-system diagnostics and the publisher’s named endpoints are sufficient for an initial support case. If no valid match endpoint is available, state that limitation instead of pretending a route to the game’s marketing site represents the session.

sections.heading: Test the connection under ordinary household load
paragraphs: If lag appears when someone uploads files, begins a video call or downloads a large update, reproduce that ordinary load once in a controlled way and compare it with the idle baseline. Record which activity started and when the game metrics changed. Queues in a router or access link can increase latency under load even when advertised bandwidth is high. Stop the load immediately if it disrupts another person’s work or a metered connection. The objective is correlation, not stress testing the household network.

Check both upload and download activity. Cloud photo backup, livestreaming and file synchronization can fill the upstream path while remaining less visible than a download. Use the router’s own traffic view only if already available and understood; do not install unknown monitoring software or capture other people’s content. A timestamped note that latency rises during a known upload is often enough for the next step, such as scheduling transfers or consulting the router or provider documentation.

sections.heading: Distinguish a local problem from a game-server incident
paragraphs: Compare signals that use different paths. If several unrelated services fail on the same device and other household devices also struggle, investigate the local network or provider first. If only one title and one region fail while ordinary browsing and another game remain stable, check the publisher’s official status page and support channels. Do not treat social-media speculation as confirmation. Record the status page time and incident identifier when one exists.

A server incident can coexist with local Wi-Fi weakness. Likewise, a good general speed test cannot prove that a particular game route is healthy. Report what each observation supports: local radio instability, load-related delay, broad internet trouble, title-specific failure or inconclusive evidence. Avoid absolute language such as “the server is definitely broken” unless the publisher confirms the incident. This disciplined wording makes a support ticket easier to act on.

sections.heading: Avoid risky fixes that destroy the diagnostic value
paragraphs: Do not disable the firewall, antivirus or router security to see whether lag disappears. Do not place the gaming PC in a public DMZ or forward broad port ranges copied from an unofficial forum. These changes can increase exposure and create a new variable without proving the original cause. If a publisher’s official guide requires a specific network change, record the original setting, apply only the documented scope, and reverse it if the test fails or support no longer needs it.

A DNS change usually affects name resolution, not the ongoing latency of every established game session. It may alter which service endpoint is selected, but it is not a universal packet-loss repair. Similarly, reinstalling the game rarely repairs congestion between the router and a remote server. Preserve the baseline before updates or resets. Make one reversible change at a time, retest the same scenario and stop when the evidence contradicts the hypothesis.

sections.heading: Create a privacy-safe report for support
paragraphs: Prepare a short manifest containing the game and build, server region, local time with time zone, connection type, symptom, idle baseline, loaded comparison and Ethernet-versus-Wi-Fi result when available. Attach only the relevant network overlay screenshot and the smallest diagnostic output requested by official support. Remove chat, player names, account identifiers, device names and private addresses when they are not required. Keep an untouched private original and label every redacted copy.

Send the report through the publisher’s authenticated portal, the platform’s official support system or the internet provider’s documented channel. Avoid public paste sites for route output and logs. State limitations plainly: for example, the match server address was unavailable, the issue could not be reproduced safely, or the test used a different time window. A precise incomplete report is more trustworthy than a large archive that implies certainty the evidence does not provide.

sections.heading: Retest once and close the investigation cleanly
paragraphs: After the support team, provider or player makes one justified change, repeat the same scenario and measurement window. Compare symptom frequency, latency variation and loss rather than declaring success because one match felt better. If the problem disappears, keep the before-and-after notes until the ticket closes. If it returns, add a new timestamped observation; do not edit the original result to make the narrative look cleaner.

Stop collecting once the evidence consistently identifies the failing layer or official support accepts the case. Continuous diagnostics can consume attention and expose more network information than necessary. Restore any temporary logging, reconnect normal household activity and document the final outcome. If the incident was confirmed on the publisher side, link the official notice. If it remained inconclusive, say so and preserve the packet for the next recurrence instead of inventing a cause.

items.title: How to Back Up PC Game Saves Before Reinstalling Windows
items.dek: A practical, evidence-first backup plan for Steam, Epic, Xbox app, GOG and standalone PC games—without assuming that every cloud icon protects every local save.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original editorial illustration showing a PC game save folder copied to two verified backup destinations before a Windows reinstall
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original editorial artwork with no third-party logos or game assets
body: Before reinstalling Windows, make two independent copies of every save you care about: one copy of the game's actual local save folder and one tested backup on a separate device or trusted storage service. Confirm cloud-sync status, close the game and launcher, copy the files, record their original paths, and open at least one copied folder. Cloud saves are useful, but they are not proof that every title, profile, screenshot, mod or configuration file is protected.

A clean Windows installation can solve deep system problems, but it also removes local data that launchers do not manage. Some games synchronize saves; others synchronize only selected files, and older or standalone titles may keep everything locally. A cloud icon can also represent an old revision, a conflict or a sync that never finished. The safe approach is therefore to identify each game's storage method, preserve the local files, verify the copies and only then erase or format anything.

This guide covers ordinary PC game saves and settings. It does not recommend bypassing encryption, DRM or account security, and it cannot recover data that has already been securely erased. File paths and launcher behavior change, so use each publisher's current documentation for the final decision. If a drive is failing, clicking or disappearing, minimize writes and seek professional recovery advice instead of repeatedly scanning or reinstalling it.
takeaways: Treat launcher cloud sync as one layer, not as the only backup.
Close games and launchers before copying files so the backup is internally consistent.
Record the original path, game version, account and date beside every save folder.
Keep two copies on different storage locations and verify at least one before reinstalling Windows.

sections.heading: Start with an inventory, not a blind folder copy
paragraphs: List the games with progress that would be painful to lose. Include more than the titles installed today: early-access games, emulators, standalone downloads and games you removed but may have left saves behind. For each entry, record the launcher or store, the Windows user account that played it, whether the game advertises cloud synchronization, and the last time the save was opened. This inventory prevents the common mistake of backing up only the biggest installation folders while missing the small save folders that actually matter.

Separate replaceable program data from personal state. Game executables and downloaded assets can usually be reinstalled; saves, custom maps, replays, screenshots, controller profiles and locally stored mods may not be replaceable. Do not assume the save lives beside the executable. Modern games commonly use Documents, Saved Games, AppData or a publisher-specific folder, while older games may write into their installation directory. The inventory should therefore name the exact item to preserve, not merely the drive on which the game is installed.

sections.heading: Confirm what the launcher cloud actually covers
paragraphs: Open the launcher while online and check the individual game's synchronization status. Steam explains that Steam Cloud can store game and platform data, but availability and implementation are set per game. Xbox cloud saves depend on the Xbox network and the title's support. GOG Galaxy offers cloud saves for supported games. A launcher-wide feature page is not evidence that a particular title has uploaded the latest local file, so inspect the game's page, settings or publisher documentation and note the time of the last successful synchronization.

Resolve conflicts before making the backup. If a launcher asks whether to keep a local or cloud version, stop and compare dates, file sizes and the progress visible in the game. Do not click the newest-looking choice without checking the machine's clock and the actual save. Launch the game once, confirm the correct slot, exit normally and allow synchronization to finish. Then close the launcher. This produces a known state and avoids copying one version while the service later overwrites it with another.

sections.heading: Find the real local save path
paragraphs: Begin with the publisher's support page, the game's documentation or its launcher page. When official information is absent, PCGamingWiki can be a useful secondary directory for common save locations, but verify the path on your own system. Typical roots include the user's Documents folder, Saved Games, AppData Local, AppData LocalLow, AppData Roaming, ProgramData and a launcher userdata directory. Hidden folders may need to be shown in File Explorer. Never enable broad permission changes merely to expose a folder.

Identify the save by content and timing. After closing the game, inspect the candidate directory for files modified at the time of the last save. A folder that contains only shader caches, logs or downloaded assets is not enough. Some titles split progress, settings and screenshots across several locations, and some use a numeric account identifier. Copy the parent folder when it is reasonably small so metadata and companion files remain together. Record the full original path in a text file stored beside the backup.

sections.heading: Close every process that can still write to the save
paragraphs: Exit the game through its menu and wait for any saving indicator to disappear. Quit the launcher as well, including its notification-area process if it continues running. For games with dedicated mod managers, cloud agents or companion utilities, close those programs after they finish their own work. Copying while a process is writing can capture an incomplete database, a temporary file or mismatched parts of a multi-file save. A normal shutdown is safer than ending the process abruptly.

Do not start a Windows reinstall immediately after a crash. Reopen the game first if it can be done safely, confirm that the wanted save loads, exit cleanly and then copy. If the game is already unstable, preserve the existing folder before attempting repairs, because verification, rollback or a new launch may modify it. Label that first copy as pre-repair. You can make a second copy after the game works, but the untouched version gives recovery tools and support staff a better reference.

sections.heading: Make two independent backup copies
paragraphs: Create a dated folder such as Game-Saves-2026-10-18 and place one subfolder per game inside it. Copy the identified save, configuration and user-content folders without changing their internal names. Add a small manifest containing the title, launcher, account nickname without passwords, original path, game version if known and backup time. This context matters months later when several folders have generic names such as SaveGames or Profiles and when a new installation creates a different account-number directory.

Store the completed backup in two separate places. One can be an external drive or another computer; the second can be a reputable cloud-storage account you already use. Two folders on the same physical SSD are not independent backups, and a partition on the disk you plan to erase can disappear with it. If the saves contain personal names, chat logs or custom images, consider encrypted storage supported by your operating system or provider. Never put account passwords or recovery codes in the manifest.

sections.heading: Verify the copy before you trust it
paragraphs: Open the backup destination and confirm that the expected subfolders and files are present. Compare the item count and total size with the source, allowing for ordinary filesystem differences. Open the manifest and a harmless text or image file from the destination rather than the source. For especially valuable saves, create a cryptographic checksum list with a trusted tool and preserve it beside the copy. A checksum proves that a later file matches the backed-up bytes; it does not prove that the game can interpret a logically corrupted save.

Test restoration when practical. On a second Windows account, another machine, or a temporary folder documented by the game, copy one noncritical save and confirm that the game recognizes it. Avoid experiments that risk replacing the only good cloud version. If a full restore test is not feasible, at minimum disconnect the backup device, reconnect it, navigate to the files and verify their dates and sizes again. The goal is evidence that the destination works independently, not a progress bar that once reached 100 percent.

sections.heading: Use File History carefully and understand its scope
paragraphs: Microsoft File History can back up versions of files in selected libraries and folders to another drive or network location. It is useful as an additional layer when the relevant save path is included, but many AppData locations are not automatically covered by a user's ordinary library choices. Review the folders that File History protects and verify that a version of the actual save can be browsed. Do not assume that enabling the feature immediately before reinstalling captures every hidden game directory.

File History is not a disk image and it is not a substitute for the manual game inventory. System images, OneDrive folder backup and third-party tools each protect different scopes. Use only software you already trust and understand, and make sure the recovery process is documented. Whatever tool you choose, retain the direct copied folders as a portable fallback. Proprietary backup containers can be useful, but a plain verified copy is easier to inspect when the original Windows installation is gone.

sections.heading: Back up mods, profiles and screenshots separately
paragraphs: Mods can depend on an exact game build, script extender, load order and manager database. Copying only the mod files may not reproduce the environment. Export a mod list or profile through the manager's supported feature, save configuration files and note the game version. Do not redistribute paid or copyrighted mod assets. After reinstalling, restore the manager and compatible tools from their official sources before reintroducing the profile. A save created with missing content can load incorrectly or become permanently altered.

Screenshots, photo-mode exports, custom maps, replays and controller layouts may be stored outside the save directory. Launchers can upload some screenshots without retaining every original file or edit. Search the game's settings and the launcher capture folder, then add these items to the inventory. If a replay requires a specific game version, keep that note beside it. Treat locally created content as personal data even when the gameplay progress itself is already synchronized.

sections.heading: Prepare the reinstall without erasing the evidence
paragraphs: Before booting installation media, confirm that both backup destinations are disconnected from the disk operation and that you know which physical drive will be erased. Check the Windows edition, account access and recovery information using Microsoft's official guidance. Do not leave the only external backup attached while deleting partitions; similar drive sizes and labels can cause destructive mistakes. Photograph or write down the target disk model if that helps distinguish it in the installer.

Keep the inventory available on another device. It should list the launchers to reinstall, the games with local saves and the destination of each backup. Avoid downloading unofficial all-in-one game packs or save-transfer utilities after Windows returns. Install Windows updates, hardware drivers and launchers from official sources. Sign in with the intended account before restoring numeric launcher folders, because a different account may generate a different directory and sync context.

sections.heading: Restore one game at a time
paragraphs: Install the launcher and game, run the title once to create its current folder structure, then exit it completely. Compare the newly created path with the recorded original. If the game supports cloud saves, let the launcher report its state but do not allow an empty new save to overwrite a known-good backup without reviewing the conflict. Copy the backed-up files into the documented location while the game and launcher are closed, preserving the new empty folder as a rollback if necessary.

Launch the game offline only when the publisher permits it and when doing so will not create a licensing or synchronization problem. Check the slot name, play time and in-game position. Exit normally, reconnect if needed and resolve any cloud prompt deliberately. Once the restored save has synchronized successfully, mark that game complete in the inventory. This paced approach contains mistakes: if one game's path has changed, you can correct it without mixing that problem with ten other simultaneous restores.

sections.heading: Know what not to copy back
paragraphs: Do not blindly restore old executables, DLL files, anti-cheat components, driver files or entire Program Files trees. These can be incompatible with the clean operating system and may reintroduce the fault that motivated the reinstall. Reinstall program components from official sources. Restore only the documented user state and custom content. If a save folder contains caches, logs and temporary downloads, prefer the narrower supported files unless the publisher says the whole directory is portable.

Scan removable media with the security tools built into the updated system before opening unknown executable content. A backup preserves whatever existed at the time, including potentially unwanted files. Be especially cautious with abandoned mod installers and community tools obtained years ago. The point of a clean reinstall is to re-establish a trusted software base while recovering personal progress, not to reconstruct every undocumented binary from the old machine.

sections.heading: A final pre-erase checklist
paragraphs: Do not erase the old installation until every important game appears in the inventory; cloud status has been checked; the game and launcher were closed; local paths were copied; two independent destinations exist; the manifest records the original locations; and at least one destination was reopened and inspected. Verify screenshots, replays, mods and controller profiles separately. Confirm account recovery access without storing passwords in the backup. Disconnect the external copy before launching the installer.

After the reinstall, keep the backup unchanged until the restored saves have loaded and synchronized across several sessions. Then retain at least one archive for a reasonable period rather than deleting both copies immediately. The same method becomes a reusable maintenance habit: update the inventory after major campaigns or creative projects, test cloud sync before travel, and periodically verify the external copy. A backup is not a product you buy once; it is evidence that your irreplaceable game state can survive the next failure.

items.title: PS5 DualSense Stick Drift: How to Diagnose It Before Paying for Repair
items.dek: A practical evidence-first checklist for unwanted PS5 controller movement: compare games, test dead zones, update firmware and decide when repair makes sense.
